messages:
maria: Heads up - we got a report from QA that our sample app hangs on large streaming responses after network flaps. Looks like coroutine jobs never finish and UI shows spinner forever. Anyone seen Retrofit + OkHttp cancellation weirdness on Android? :thinking:

alex: Yup. Often it's callTimeout vs readTimeout confusion. callTimeout cancels the entire Call, but if you're wrapping in a Coroutine and using withTimeout, the okhttp call may still hold sockets open unless you propagate cancellation properly.

maria: Repro steps I saw: 1) Start streaming endpoint (chunked) 2) Kill wifi 3) Wait ~10s 4) Re-enable wifi 5) UI stuck and logs show "socket read timeout" but coroutine job is active.

tony: Do you use OkHttp's Call.cancel() when coroutine is cancelled? If you use execute() on background thread it won't auto-cancel. For suspend functions with Call.await() helpers, you need to register cancellation to call.cancel().

ciara: We had a similar on Android 14 where Thread.interrupt() behavior changed for some socket read impls. The safe pattern: attach invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() } to the coroutine job and prefer call.timeout() (OkHttp 4.10+) to set per-call timeouts rather than global readTimeout.

alex: Example (Kotlin):
```
val call = okHttpClient.newCall(request)
val job = coroutineContext[Job]
job?.invokeOnCompletion { if (it is CancellationException) call.cancel() }
val resp = suspendCancellableCoroutine<Response> { cont ->
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() }
  call.enqueue(object: Callback { ... })
}
```
That pattern reliably cancels sockets on coroutine cancel.

maria: We're using retrofit's CallAdapter to return Deferred. Maybe that's the culprit. Any quick fixes?

tony: If you control the adapter, switch to suspend functions (retrofit 2.6+) or ensure Deferred is cancelled -> call.cancel. Lots of older adapters forgot to wire cancellation through.

alex: Also check OkHttp Dispatcher queue: if dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost is default 5 and your retries spike after connectivity, you can deadlock if all worker threads are blocked. We fixed a leak by increasing maxRequests and using asynchronous enqueue instead of blocking execute.

ciara: For streaming endpoints consider chunked response handling: process bytes on a dedicated IO coroutine with a timeout per-chunk. That avoids a single long read preventing cancellation checks.

maria: Good notes. QA also saw the sample app hang only when using the sample SDK config (we set readTimeout=0 for infinite streaming). Maybe that's the issue.

tony: readTimeout=0 disables heartbeat checks and can hide network loss. Use call.timeout(). Also set pingInterval for HTTP/2 to keep connections alive, and a ConnectionPool with keepAliveDuration that suits mobile.

alex: For tests, simulate flaky network with: `adb shell svc wifi disable; sleep 8; adb shell svc wifi enable`. Also Robolectric doesn't handle real sockets, use emulator + fiddler or network-link-conditioner.

maria: Action items: 1) Add cancellation wiring in Retrofit CallAdapter -> call.cancel on Deferred cancel 2) Prefer suspend functions in examples 3) Add note in sample app about not using readTimeout=0 and instead use call.timeout + per-chunk timeouts 4) Add small e2e test on emulator that toggles wifi and asserts coroutine job completes.

ci-bot: ci/test-run streaming-cancel-sanity started for branch fix/streaming-cancel-228

ciara: I'll PR the CallAdapter fix and update docs. Assigning myself to sample app changes.

tony: One extra gotcha: OkHttp's connectionPool eviction thread may close idle connections during background doze, reopening can be slow. Consider keeping lightweight keepalive pings or fallbacks to retry with exponential backoff and small jitter.

maria: Perfect, thanks all! Will attach QA traces to the ticket and mark flaky label. :+1:
